jp: 誰[だれ]{が|ga-question}この質問[しつもん]{に|ni-target}答[こた]えましたか。
en: Who answered this question?
why: A question word standing as the subject is the unknown itself, so it takes が.

jp: どの授業[じゅぎょう]{が|ga-question}一番[いちばん]おもしろいですか。
en: Which class is the most interesting?
why: どの picks one from a set, so the question word is the subject and takes が.

jp: 誰[だれ]{が|ga-question}教室[きょうしつ]{の|no-possessive}窓[まど]{を|o-object}開[あ]けましたか。
en: Who opened the classroom window?
why: A question word standing as the subject is the unknown itself, so it takes が.

jp: 教科[きょうか]{の|no-possessive}中[なか]{で|de-scope}何[なに]{が|ga-question}一番[いちばん]好[す]きですか。
en: Which subject do you like best?
why: 何 is the unknown being asked about, so it takes が, not は.

jp: 会議[かいぎ]{に|ni-destination}誰[だれ]{が|ga-question}来[き]ますか。
en: Who is coming to the meeting?
why: A question word standing as the subject is the unknown itself, so it takes が.

jp: 誰[だれ]{が|ga-question}一番[いちばん]早[はや]く会社[かいしゃ]{に|ni-destination}着[つ]きましたか。
en: Who arrived at the office first?
why: A question word standing as the subject is the unknown itself, so it takes が.

jp: 誰[だれ]{が|ga-question}黒板[こくばん]{を|o-object}消[け]しましたか。鈴木[すずき]さん{が|ga-subject}消[け]しました。
en: "Who erased the blackboard?" "Mr. Suzuki did."
why: The answer to a 誰 question is the new information, so it takes が.

jp: 今日[きょう]、誰[だれ]{が|ga-question}掃除[そうじ]{を|o-object}しますか。田中[たなか]さん{が|ga-subject}します。
en: "Who is cleaning today?" "Ms. Tanaka is."
why: Naming the person who fills the gap in a 誰 question is new information, so が.

jp: 教室[きょうしつ]{に|ni-location}誰[だれ]{が|ga-question}いますか。
en: Who is in the classroom?
why: A question word standing as the subject is the unknown itself, so it takes が.

jp: 田中[たなか]さん{は|wa-topic}どの教科[きょうか]{が|ga-question}好[す]きですか。
en: Which subject does Mr. Tanaka like?
why: どの教科 is the unknown being asked about, so it takes が; Mr. Tanaka is the topic.

jp: 英語[えいご]{と|to-and}日本語[にほんご]{と|to-and}、どちら{が|ga-question}好[す]きですか。
en: Which do you like better, English or Japanese?
why: どちら asks which of two, so the question word takes が.

jp: 数学[すうがく]{と|to-and}理科[りか]{と|to-and}、どちら{が|ga-question}得意[とくい]ですか。
en: Which are you better at, math or science?
why: どちら is the unknown in a choice question, so it takes が.

jp: あ、チャイム{が|ga-subject}鳴[な]っています{よ|yo-assertion}。
en: Oh, the bell is ringing!
why: You are pointing out something that has just happened, so the subject takes が.

jp: 見[み]て、黒板[こくばん]{に|ni-location}変[へん]な絵[え]{が|ga-subject}描[か]いてあります。
en: Look, there is a strange picture drawn on the blackboard.
why: A new thing you have just noticed is the subject of the sentence, so が.

jp: 突然[とつぜん]、教室[きょうしつ]{の|no-possessive}電気[でんき]{が|ga-subject}消[き]えました。
en: Suddenly the lights in the classroom went out.
why: A sudden event is reported as news, and the subject of the news takes が.

jp: 昨日[きのう]、学校[がっこう]{の|no-possessive}近[ちか]く{で|de-place}事故[じこ]{が|ga-subject}ありました。
en: There was an accident near the school yesterday.
why: The accident is introduced for the first time, so it takes が.

jp: 来月[らいげつ]、新[あたら]しい留学生[りゅうがくせい]{が|ga-subject}クラス{に|ni-target}入[はい]ります。
en: Next month a new exchange student will join the class.
why: A person being introduced for the first time takes が.

jp: ほら、雨[あめ]{が|ga-subject}降[ふ]ってきました{よ|yo-assertion}。
en: Look, it has started to rain!
why: Pointing out something you can see happening right now takes が.

jp: 今朝[けさ]、会社[かいしゃ]{に|ni-destination}知[し]らない人[ひと]{が|ga-subject}来[き]ました{よ|yo-assertion}。
en: A stranger came to the office this morning, you know.
why: A person newly brought into the conversation takes が.

jp: 授業中[じゅぎょうちゅう]、後[うし]ろ{の|no-possessive}席[せき]{で|de-place}誰[だれ]か{が|ga-subject}くしゃみ{を|o-object}しました。
en: During class, someone in the seat behind me sneezed.
why: An unspecified someone (誰か) doing something is new information, so it takes が.

jp: 先生[せんせい]{が/の|ga-sub-clause}書[か]いた本[ほん]{は|wa-topic}とても有名[ゆうめい]です。
en: The book the teacher wrote is very famous.
why: Inside a clause that modifies a noun the subject takes が, never は.

jp: 兄[あに]{が/の|ga-sub-clause}使[つか]っていた辞書[じしょ]{を|o-object}、私[わたし]{は/が|wa-topic}今[いま]使[つか]っています。
en: I am now using the dictionary my brother used to use.
why: The subject of a relative clause takes が.

jp: 授業[じゅぎょう]{が|ga-sub-clause}終[お]わったら、図書館[としょかん]{に|ni-destination}行[い]きます。
en: When class is over, I will go to the library.
why: The subject of a conditional clause takes が.

jp: 雨[あめ]{が|ga-sub-clause}降[ふ]るとき、バス{で|de-means}学校[がっこう]{に/へ|ni-destination}行[い]きます。
en: When it rains, I go to school by bus.
why: The subject of a とき clause takes が.

jp: 母[はは]{が|ga-sub-clause}帰[かえ]る前[まえ]{に|ni-time}、宿題[しゅくだい]{を|o-object}しておきます。
en: I will do my homework before my mother gets home.
why: The subject of a 前に clause takes が.

jp: 先生[せんせい]{が|ga-sub-clause}教[おし]えてくれたこと{を|o-object}ノート{に|ni-target}書[か]きました。
en: I wrote in my notebook what the teacher taught me.
why: The subject inside the clause modifying こと takes が.

jp: 友達[ともだち]{が|ga-sub-clause}おすすめしてくれた参考書[さんこうしょ]{を|o-object}買[か]いました。
en: I bought the reference book my friend recommended.
why: The subject of a relative clause takes が.

jp: 彼[かれ]{が/の|ga-sub-clause}作[つく]った資料[しりょう]{は/が|wa-topic}とても分[わ]かりやすいです。
en: The materials he made are very easy to understand.
why: The subject of a relative clause takes が.

jp: 試験[しけん]{が|ga-sub-clause}近[ちか]い{ので|node-because}、毎晩[まいばん]勉強[べんきょう]しています。
en: Because the exam is near, I study every night.
why: The subject of a ので clause takes が.

jp: 部長[ぶちょう]{が|ga-sub-clause}出張[しゅっちょう]{に|ni-purpose}行[い]っている間[あいだ]{に|ni-time}、資料[しりょう]{を|o-object}作[つく]ります。
en: While the manager is away on a business trip, I will make the materials.
why: The subject of a 間に clause takes が.

jp: 子供[こども]{が|ga-sub-clause}学校[がっこう]{に/へ|ni-destination}行[い]っている間[あいだ]、母[はは]{は/が|wa-topic}会社[かいしゃ]{で|de-place}働[はたら]いています。
en: While the children are at school, my mother works at the office.
why: The subject of a 間 clause takes が.

jp: 先生[せんせい]{が|ga-sub-clause}来[く]る前[まえ]{に|ni-time}、席[せき]{に|ni-target}座[すわ]ってください。
en: Please sit down before the teacher arrives.
why: The subject of a 前に clause takes が.

jp: 教室[きょうしつ]{に|ni-location}学生[がくせい]{が|ga-existence}三人[さんにん]います。
en: There are three students in the classroom.
why: Saying that something exists introduces it as new, so it takes が.

jp: 机[つくえ]{の|no-possessive}上[うえ]{に|ni-location}辞書[じしょ]{が|ga-existence}あります。
en: There is a dictionary on the desk.
why: With ある or いる the thing that exists takes が.

jp: 図書館[としょかん]{に|ni-location}日本語[にほんご]{の|no-possessive}新聞[しんぶん]{が|ga-existence}ありますか。
en: Does the library have Japanese newspapers?
why: The thing whose existence is asked about takes が.

jp: 会社[かいしゃ]{の|no-possessive}近[ちか]く{に|ni-location}おいしい食堂[しょくどう]{が|ga-existence}あります。
en: There is a good cafeteria near the company.
why: An existence sentence introduces the new thing with が.

jp: 学校[がっこう]{の|no-possessive}前[まえ]{に|ni-location}コンビニ{が|ga-subject}できました。
en: A convenience store opened in front of the school.
why: The new store is reported as a fresh fact, so it takes が.

jp: 会社[かいしゃ]{の|no-possessive}前[まえ]{に|ni-location}大[おお]きいトラック{が|ga-subject}止[と]まっています。
en: A big truck is parked in front of the company.
why: Something newly noticed in a place takes が.

jp: 町[まち]{に|ni-location}図書館[としょかん]{が|ga-existence}あります。その図書館[としょかん]{は|wa-topic}夜[よる]九時[くじ]{まで|made-until}開[あ]いています。
en: There is a library in the town. That library is open until nine at night.
why: The library was just introduced, so the second sentence makes it the known topic with は.

jp: 会社[かいしゃ]{の|no-possessive}隣[となり]{に|ni-location}小[ちい]さい公園[こうえん]{が|ga-existence}あります。その公園[こうえん]{は|wa-topic}とても静[しず]かです。
en: There is a small park next to the company. That park is very quiet.
why: First mention of the park in an existence sentence takes が; the second sentence will use は.

jp: 駅[えき]{の|no-possessive}前[まえ]{に|ni-location}本屋[ほんや]{が|ga-existence}あります。その本屋[ほんや]{は|wa-topic}日曜日[にちようび]{も|mo-also}開[あ]いています。
en: There is a bookstore in front of the station. That bookstore is open on Sundays too.
why: The bookstore is already known from the first sentence, so it becomes the topic with は.

jp: 教室[きょうしつ]{の|no-possessive}外[そと]{から|kara-from}生徒[せいと]{の|no-possessive}声[こえ]{が|ga-sense}聞[き]こえます。
en: I can hear the students' voices from outside the classroom.
why: What you can hear or see with 聞こえる・見える takes が.

jp: 窓[まど]{から|kara-from}校庭[こうてい]{が|ga-sense}見[み]えます。
en: You can see the schoolyard from the window.
why: The thing that can be seen with 見える takes が.

jp: 隣[となり]{の|no-possessive}教室[きょうしつ]{から|kara-from}変[へん]な音[おと]{が|ga-sense}します。
en: A strange noise is coming from the next classroom.
why: A sound that is perceived with 音がする takes が.

jp: 科目[かもく]{の|no-possessive}中[なか]{で|de-scope}、歴史[れきし]{が|ga-stative}一番[いちばん]好[す]きです。
en: Among the subjects, I like history best.
why: Picking the one you like best out of a set takes が on the chosen item.

jp: これ{は|wa-topic}日本語[にほんご]{の|no-possessive}教科書[きょうかしょ]です。
en: This is a Japanese textbook.
why: これ is something already in front of both people, so it is the topic with は.

jp: あの教室[きょうしつ]{の|no-possessive}前[まえ]{に|ni-location}いる人[ひと]{は|wa-topic}誰[だれ]ですか。
en: Who is the person in front of that classroom?
why: The person is already in view; you ask about the known topic with は.

jp: 日本語[にほんご]{の|no-possessive}試験[しけん]{は|wa-topic}いつですか。
en: When is the Japanese exam?
why: The exam is already known, so it is the topic and the question word comes last.

jp: 会議[かいぎ]{は|wa-topic}何時[なんじ]{から|kara-from}ですか。
en: What time does the meeting start?
why: The meeting is the known topic you ask about, so は.

jp: あの人[ひと]{を|o-object}知[し]っていますか。はい、あの人[ひと]{は|wa-topic}大学[だいがく]{の|no-possessive}先生[せんせい]です。
en: "Do you know that person?" "Yes, that person is a university professor."
why: The person has just been mentioned, so in the answer it becomes the topic with は.

jp: 会社[かいしゃ]{の|no-possessive}会議室[かいぎしつ]{は|wa-topic}どこですか。
en: Where is the company's meeting room?
why: The meeting room is the known topic of a where-question, so は.

jp: 田中[たなか]さん{は|wa-topic}どの人[ひと]ですか。
en: Which person is Mr. Tanaka?
why: Mr. Tanaka is the topic and どの人 is the answer being asked for.

jp: 先生[せんせい]{の|no-possessive}お名前[なまえ]{は|wa-topic}何[なん]ですか。
en: What is the teacher's name?
why: The name is the topic being asked about, so は.

jp: 新[あたら]しい社長[しゃちょう]{は|wa-topic}どんな人[ひと]ですか。
en: What kind of person is the new president?
why: The new president is the known topic you ask about, so は.

jp: お仕事[しごと]{は|wa-topic}何[なん]ですか。
en: What is your job?
why: The job is the topic of the question and 何 is the answer asked for.

jp: 昼休[ひるやす]み{は|wa-topic}十二時[じゅうにじ]{から|kara-from}一時[いちじ]{まで|made-until}です。
en: Lunch break is from twelve to one.
why: The lunch break is the known topic and the times are the comment.

jp: 来週[らいしゅう]{の|no-possessive}会議[かいぎ]{は|wa-topic}会議室[かいぎしつ]{で|de-place}あります。
en: Next week's meeting will be held in the meeting room.
why: The meeting is the known topic, and the sentence says where it takes place.

jp: この漢字[かんじ]{は|wa-topic}何[なん]{と|to-quote}読[よ]みますか。
en: How do you read this kanji?
why: The kanji in front of you is the topic with は; 何と読みますか is the question about it.

jp: 今日[きょう]{は|wa-topic}天気[てんき]{が/は|ga-subject}いいです{ね|ne-agreement}。
en: The weather is nice today, isn't it?
why: 今日 sets the time frame as the topic; it cannot be the subject marked by が.

jp: 今日[きょう]{は|wa-topic}授業[じゅぎょう]{が/は|ga-existence}ありません。
en: There are no classes today.
why: 今日 sets the time frame as the topic; it cannot be the subject marked by が.

jp: この本[ほん]{は|wa-topic}昨日[きのう]図書館[としょかん]{で|de-place}借[か]りました。
en: I borrowed this book at the library yesterday.
why: The object this book is brought forward as the topic with は; が cannot mark it here.

jp: 宿題[しゅくだい]{は|wa-topic}もう先生[せんせい]{に|ni-recipient}出[だ]しました。
en: I have already handed the homework in to the teacher.
why: The homework is the topic picked up as an object, so it takes は, not が.

jp: 新[あたら]しい辞書[じしょ]{は|wa-topic}まだ買[か]っていません。
en: I have not bought the new dictionary yet.
why: The object is brought forward as the topic, so は; が would not fit 買う here.

jp: 報告書[ほうこくしょ]{は|wa-topic}部長[ぶちょう]{に|ni-recipient}送[おく]りました。
en: I sent the report to the manager.
why: The report is the topic picked up as an object, so は.

jp: 宿題[しゅくだい]{は|wa-topic}金曜日[きんようび]{までに|madeni-deadline}出[だ]してください。
en: Please hand in the homework by Friday.
why: The homework is the object brought forward as the topic, so は.

jp: 月曜日[げつようび]{は|wa-contrast}授業[じゅぎょう]{が|ga-existence}ありますが、火曜日[かようび]{は|wa-contrast}ありません。
en: There are classes on Monday, but on Tuesday there are none.
why: Two days are set against each other, so は marks the contrast; が would say Tuesday does not exist.

jp: 土曜日[どようび]{は/に|wa-contrast}学校[がっこう]{に/へ|ni-destination}行[い]きますが、日曜日[にちようび]{は|wa-contrast}行[い]きません。
en: I go to school on Saturdays, but not on Sundays.
why: Setting Sunday against Saturday calls for contrastive は.

jp: 宿題[しゅくだい]{を/は|o-object}しましたが、予習[よしゅう]{は|wa-contrast}しませんでした。
en: I did the homework, but I did not do the preparation.
why: は sets the preparation against the homework; が cannot mark the object of しない.

jp: 資料[しりょう]{を/は|o-object}読[よ]みましたが、メール{は|wa-contrast}まだ読[よ]んでいません。
en: I read the materials, but I have not read the e-mail yet.
why: は contrasts the e-mail with the materials; が would be ungrammatical for this object.

jp: 食堂[しょくどう]{で|de-place}カレー{を|o-object}食[た]べましたが、サラダ{は|wa-contrast}食[た]べませんでした。
en: I ate curry at the cafeteria, but I did not eat the salad.
why: は contrasts the salad with the curry; が cannot mark the object of 食べる.
